exposure: Type of uterine rupture (complete vs. partial)
Number of previous cesarean sections (more than two)
cohort: The study included 112 uterine rupture cases (29 complete and 83 partial) from the Women's Hospital of the University of Cologne between October 2010 and January 2021.
finding: Complete uterine ruptures were associated with significantly higher risks of severe maternal and neonatal adverse outcomes compared to partial uterine ruptures, with previous vaginal birth and abdominal pain identified as key risk factors for complete rupture.
mod_finding: Previous vaginal birth significantly increased the risk of complete uterine rupture (OR=7.14), as did a previous cesarean section (OR=4.94), while more than two previous cesarean sections showed a reduced risk (OR=0.66).
